title: Cache-key normalization, probabilistic TTL synthesis, and staged rollback playbook
creator: Ayesha Khan
description: Goal: Produce a reproducible, automated workflow for deriving per-prefix cache TTLs and cache-key normalization rules using probabilistic hit-rate synthesis, and ship a safe staged rollout with automatic rollback heuristics. Motivation: current manual TTL and key-design changes cause regressions in cost and latency when applied at scale. We will build a simulator + optimizer that (1) consumes prefix telemetry and request traces, (2) synthesizes TTL recommendations with uncertainty estimates, (3) outputs a compact policy and normalization ruleset, and (4) applies changes via a staged feature-flag rollout with automatic rollback triggers.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end pipeline: telemetry -> model -> recommended policy JSON produced automatically
Simulator can replay 30 days of traffic and compute estimated cost delta and latency impact with confidence intervals
Staged rollout system applies policy to 1%, 10%, 50%, 100% buckets with health gates at each stage
Automated rollback triggers if cost increases >5% or 95th latency increases >10% or error-rate increases >0.2% for 10 minutes
Documentation and runbook added to Confluence with example policy and troubleshooting steps
decision_log: 2026-02-25: Chose Bayesian hierarchical model for TTL estimation to share strength across sparse prefixes and provide calibrated uncertainty (decision by @Miguel)
2026-03-02: Selected LRU+segmented hotset for runtime eviction; decided not to change eviction at rollout to reduce moving parts (@Ayesha)
2026-03-07: Agreed to canonicalize cache keys by template fingerprinting and deterministic hashing instead of full request body hashing to reduce cardinality and improve hit-rate stability
rollout_plan: 1) Generate baseline: collect 30 days request traces and prefix frequency histogram. 2) Run TTL synthesizer to create per-prefix TTLs plus uncertainty bands. 3) Group low-volume prefixes into 'long-tail' bucket with conservative TTL. 4) Validate via simulator: estimate token-cost savings, miss amplification, avg/95th latency delta. 5) Create compact policy file (top N prefixes + fallback policy). 6) Deploy to canary (1% traffic) behind feature flag; monitor blackbox metrics for 20 minutes. 7) If healthy, expand to 10%, then 50%, then 100% with 30m observation windows and automated health checks. 8) Automatic rollback if any gate fails or CI BQ alerts are triggered.
simulator_notes: Simulator will replay real traces while parameterizing TTLs and prefix normalization. Cost model includes: token-generation cost by model size, added latency on cache-miss (cold vs warm model), and batching efficiency loss when miss rate increases. New feature: support for knob 'prefix-splitting' where high-entropy prefixes are split into template + dynamic slot fingerprint to maximize cache reuse without over-generalizing.
cache_key_design_summary: Ruleset will implement: 1) Template extraction: parse prompt into canonical template and slot tokens using lightweight parser. 2) Slot normalization: numeric tokens truncated to magnitude bucket (e.g., 12345 -> 10000s), dates normalized to day granularity. 3) Deterministic hashing of canonical template + selected slots to a fixed-length key. 4) Reject keys exceeding cardinality threshold and route to fallback - no caching. 5) Metrics emitted per-key and per-template for hit-rate telemetry.
ttl_synthesis_algorithm: High-level: for each prefix template, estimate per-prefix arrival rate λ and observed reuse distribution. Fit a Bayesian survival model to estimate probability a cached value is still useful after t seconds. Compute expected cost(t) = miss_cost * P(miss at t) + storage_cost * (t * λ) and pick t* minimizing expected cost subject to latency constraints. For low-data prefixes, borrow posterior from similar templates via hierarchical prior. Output 90% credible interval for t*.
safety_and_rollback_heuristics: Primary gates: cost_delta > +5% (negative outcome), p95_latency > +10%, error_rate_absolute_increase > 0.2%. Secondary gates: sudden drop in kv_cache_hit_rate > 7 percentage points, telemetry lag > 2 minutes. Rollback behavior: immediate feature-flag revert to previous policy and trigger on-call page with incident runbook. After rollback, run automated diff analysis to surface likely offending keys/prefixes and propose tuned conservative TTLs.
